Name: Salve Injector
Description: Gain +1 Health after each of your next 3 games
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: A tonic injector that regenerates health over several turns; tonics are unidentified coloured tubes.
Why it fits: Qud's plainest healing tonic, and it heals over time rather than at once, which no potion here does yet. Qud's tonics are unidentified 'small coloured tubes' re-dealt every run, the same identify-by-colour game this one's potions already play.
Needs: new: healing spread over later games

Name: Ubernostrum Injector
Description: Remove every negative status and curse, then Gain +2 Health
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: The rare cure-all tonic: regeneration, removes negative effects, regrows a limb.
Why it fits: In Qud it regenerates, strips negative effects and regrows a limb: the rare full cure. Here the cure is the point (statuses and curses are what this game hangs on you), with a little healing on top.
Builds on: potions, remove_random_debuff, Scroll of Remove Curse

Name: Hulk Honey Injector
Description: Gain +2 Bash. Until your next game ends, you can't see your exact Health
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: A strength tonic that also stops you feeling pain, hiding your exact hit points.
Why it fits: Qud's strength tonic, whose catch is that you 'cannot feel pain' and lose sight of your exact hit points. Bash is this game's strength verb, and hiding the Health number is a cost the screen can actually show.
Needs: new: hiding the Health number

Name: Love Injector
Description: Drink it and you fall for the next thing you see (Lovesick). Throw it and the enemy it hits stops attacking you for 2 turns
Extra: Preference=Neutral; On Tile=the enemy on this tile won't attack you for 2 turns
What it is there: Makes the drinker love the first thing they see; injected or thrown, makes a creature follow you.
Why it fits: In Qud it makes the drinker fall in love with the first thing they look at, or, thrown or injected into a creature, makes it follow you. Potions here already have a drink half and a thrown half, and this one's two halves are opposites.
Builds on: potions' drink and throw halves, Lovesick (candidate)
Needs: new: a charmed enemy that won't attack

Name: Eaters' Nectar
Description: Gain +1 of a random verb (Bash, Dash, Push, Transmute or Scramble)
What it is there: A tonic that permanently raises a random attribute (a mutation point for a mutant).
Why it fits: Qud's permanent-attribute tonic (a random attribute for a mutant), the one injector worth saving. A permanent random stat is a Pickup relic here, like Ban Hammer, with the randomness kept.

Name: Optical Bioscanner
Description: You can see the goals of the enemies at every game next to you on the map before choosing where to go
What it is there: A face cybernetic that shows creatures' health and stats.
Why it fits: A face cybernetic that shows creatures' health and stats at a glance. Here the useful glance is ahead of time: knowing a neighbour's goals before routing there. Information relics are rare here.
Needs: new: seeing neighbours' goals before choosing

Name: Wand of Digging
Description: Dig down: move to a game one step closer to the Amulet without playing the one you're on
Extra: Charges=2; Preference=Positive
What it is there: Zapped downward it digs a hole straight to the next level; the classic escape and shortcut.
Why it fits: The game's teleports go to the start, a shop, a type or a random place; none goes TOWARD the goal, which is what digging down is.
Builds on: teleport cards (Ride the Bus, The Hermit)
Needs: new: a move that targets the Amulet's direction

Name: Wand of Sleep
Description: Every enemy in a row skips its next 2 turns
Extra: Charges=3; Preference=Positive
What it is there: A ray that puts everything in its path to sleep; bounces off walls.
Why it fits: A ray of Stun is a better wand than another damage zap, and rides the Stun status as it is.

Name: Wand of Cold
Description: Freeze a row: apply the Ice tile along it. An enemy on Ice slides one square further than it meant to
Extra: Charges=2; Preference=Positive
What it is there: A ray of cold; it freezes water and lava into walkable ice.
Why it fits: The board has two tiles (Fire, Web). Ice is the obvious third, and Wand of Fire already shows a tile-laying wand.
Needs: new: an Ice tile

Name: Scroll of Genocide
Description: Name an enemy tag: every enemy with it leaves the board, and none spawn for the rest of the run. Read cursed: the board fills with them instead
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Wipe a monster species from the game entirely; read cursed, it summons them around you ('reverse genocide').
Why it fits: One of the most famous items in roguelikes. Enemy tags already exist, so 'name a tag' is a choice the game can show; the cursed half is the scroll gamble the Preference system is for.
Needs: new: banning a tag from spawns for the run

Name: Scroll of Enchant Weapon
Description: A Weapon in your pack Gains +1 Stun for the rest of the run
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Raises your wielded weapon's enchantment by one.
Why it fits: Weapons are the newest loot kind and nothing upgrades them yet except their neighbours.

Name: Scroll of Magic Mapping
Description: Reveal the kind of every game on the map: Enemies, Event, Champion or Shop
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Maps the whole current level, secret doors included.
Why it fits: Routing is the core decision here, and a node's kind is only seen when it's offered (spec §19). Tourists start with four of these in NetHack.
Needs: new: showing node kinds beyond the offering

Name: Amulet of Life Saving
Description: The first time you would die this run, you survive at 1 Health instead; this is destroyed
What it is there: When you die wearing it, it saves you and crumbles.
Why it fits: The roguelike second life. Pieces that break on a trigger already exist (Lucky Hat, Bionic Face Plating).
Needs: new: a death-prevention trigger

Name: Bag of Holding
Description: Holds 2x2 inside, but takes one cell of the pack. Put it inside another bag and both explode, with everything in them
What it is there: The best container in the game, and famous for exploding if you put one inside another (or a wand of cancellation in it).
Why it fits: Bags give the pack its shape; one bigger inside than out is the bag every NetHack player wants, and the explosion keeps its personality.
Needs: new: a bag bigger inside than out

Name: Excalibur
Description: Stun 2 to the front. Passive: Gain +1 Luck while it is in your pack
Extra: Aim=front; Area=3x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Dip an item in a fountain or a pool; Charge=3
What it is there: The lawful hero's sword: dip a long sword into a fountain at experience level 5 or more, and the Lady of the Lake may grant it.
Why it fits: Weapons already evolve (Hero Sword into Hero Longsword); Excalibur could be the evolution of a long sword at the Fountain object. Its goal is how you get it.

Name: Unicorn Horn
Description: Use: remove a random negative status or curse
What it is there: The universal cure: apply it to fix confusion, blindness, stun, sickness and lost attributes.
Why it fits: Every NetHack player carries one. The cure is already a verb here (remove_random_debuff).

Name: Luckstone
Description: Gain +1 Luck. While this is in your pack, your Luck can't go down
What it is there: A gray stone that holds your Luck in place, so it no longer times out.
Why it fits: Joins the stone family (3 pieces) and the Luck pieces (Clover, Lucky Toe); holding Luck steady is new.
Needs: new: blocking Luck loss

Name: Skeleton Key
Description: Gain +2 Keys
What it is there: An iron key that opens locked doors, boxes and chests.
Why it fits: Keys are a stat with nothing to give or spend them (spec §4). Here is the first thing that gives them, for whenever locked paths arrive.
Needs: new: something for keys to open (locked paths, spec §4)

Name: Potion of Mutation
Description: Lose a random Buff, then gain 2 random statuses: probably good, possibly not
Extra: Preference=Neutral
What it is there: Removes 2-3 mutations, then adds 1-3 random ones (60% good) and maybe one more good one. 'A surprise in every bottle!'
Why it fits: A Neutral potion that is a real gamble rather than plain good or bad; the random-status verbs exist.

Name: Potion of Lignification
Description: Gain +4 Shields, but you can't Dash or Push until your next game
Extra: Preference=Neutral; On Tile=the enemy on this tile can't move for 2 turns
What it is there: Turns you into a tree for a while: lots of HP and resistances, but you can't move, blink or teleport.
Why it fits: Armour for mobility is a trade the verbs make visible: shields here, and the map verbs locked.
Needs: new: locking a verb for a game

Name: Scroll of Silence
Description: For 2 turns, no enemy's ability works
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Creates an aura of silence: nobody inside can cast, read, pray or shout, you included.
Why it fits: Abilities are half of what an enemy is here (spec §7.6); Wand of Cancellation strips one, this mutes them all for a while.
Needs: new: suspending abilities for N turns

Name: Scroll of Butterflies
Description: Fill the empty squares next to you with Butterfly units: they block enemies' paths and break when hit
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Summons a cloud of friendly butterflies that block attacks and knock nearby enemies back.
Why it fits: The board has one unit (Landmine); butterflies are harmless blockers, a different job from a mine.
Needs: new: a Butterfly unit

Name: Scroll of Noise
Description: Every enemy on the board takes one step toward you
Extra: Preference=Negative
What it is there: A prank scroll: a loud clang that alerts every monster nearby.
Why it fits: Scrolls need bad outcomes as much as good ones for the read-blind gamble; this one moves the board against you without hurting you.

Name: Wand of Roots
Description: Roots grab every enemy in a 3x3: they can't move for 3 turns (they can still attack)
Extra: Charges=3; Preference=Positive
What it is there: Constricts foes in a 3x3 area with grasping roots, damaging them each turn.
Why it fits: A holding wand rather than a damage one; the Web tile does the same to a single square.

Name: Sack of Spiders
Description: Use: lay the Web tile under every enemy in the front two columns
What it is there: An evocable that releases allied spiders and may web the monsters in sight.
Why it fits: The Web tile is half the board's terrain and only Sticky Bombs lay it today.

Name: Phial of Floods
Description: Use: flood a row with water. Enemies in water move one square less, and Fire on those squares goes out
What it is there: Fires a beam of water that knocks monsters back, leaves shallow water and waterlogs them.
Why it fits: A water tile would answer the Fire tile; flooding the lane the fire is in is a choice.
Needs: new: a Water tile

Name: Lightning Rod
Description: Use: 1 damage down a row. Used again in the same turn, it hits the next row too, for 2
What it is there: Its bolt grows stronger each consecutive turn you evoke it.
Why it fits: Joins the lightning family (Lightning Ring, Thunder Loop), and rewards using it twice in a row.
Needs: new: a use that grows when repeated

Name: Rune of Zot
Description: Gain +1 Key. Hold 3 and the Amulet game's boss loses 1 Damage
What it is there: Fifteen runes guard the branches; three are needed to open the Realm of Zot and reach the Orb.
Why it fits: Keys have nothing to open yet (spec §4); runes are the genre's best key, and 'three to open the end' fits the Amulet.
Needs: new: something for keys to open

Name: Scroll of Town Portal
Description: Go to the last Shop you visited, then come straight back to where you were
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: Opens a portal to town and back: the series' signature consumable.
Why it fits: The Hermit already sends you to the nearest Shop one way; the round trip is what makes a town portal.
Needs: new: a return trip

Name: The Undead Crown
Description: Whenever you defeat a boss, Gain +2 Health
What it is there: King Leoric's crown: a unique helm with life steal, his quest reward.
Why it fits: Leoric's life steal, worn by you. It carries the crown tag, which the King Bomber evolution reads (Lil' Bomber plus anything with 'crown').

Name: Griswold's Edge
Description: Push the enemy it hits back 1 and set its square on Fire
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Bring a quest item back to the person who asked for it; Charge=3
What it is there: The sword Griswold forges once you bring him the Anvil of Fury: knocks enemies back and burns them.
Why it fits: Knockback is already a weapon effect (Hero Longsword) and Fire a tile; the goal is its own quest.

Name: Chester
Description: A 3x3 bag that walks behind you instead of sitting in the pack. If an enemy reaches the front column, it hits Chester and something falls out
What it is there: A mobile chest that follows the Eye Bone and stores nine stacks of items; if it dies, it drops everything.
Why it fits: A bag with a body: storage outside the pack, at a risk. The most loved creature in the game.
Needs: new: a bag outside the pack

Name: Ham Bat
Description: Stun 3 to the front. Loses 1 Stun after every game, until it rots away
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Defeat an enemy with a weapon made of food; Charge=2
What it is there: A melee club made of meat: strong, but it spoils after 10 days.
Why it fits: A weapon that is also food: it joins both families, and spoiling is a cost the pack doesn't have yet.
Builds on: weapons, food tag (9 pieces), Stankus' Toothpick
Needs: new: loot that decays each game

Name: Tooth Trap
Description: Use: place a Tooth Trap on an empty square. An enemy that steps on it takes 1 damage and is Stunned; it re-arms after each game
What it is there: A craftable trap of hound's teeth that hits whatever steps on it; reset it after each use.
Why it fits: The board's one unit is the Landmine, which blows up; a trap you re-arm is a different job.
Needs: new: a re-arming trap unit

Name: Miner Hat
Description: You are never in darkness: immune to the Darkness curse
What it is there: A straw hat with fireflies in it that lights the way while keeping hands free.
Why it fits: The Darkness curse candidate needs an answer, and a lamp on your head is Don't Starve's.

Name: Black Candle
Description: At the start of each game, Gain +1 Shield. Events can't add curses to you. It can't be removed from your pack
What it is there: A cursed headpiece: shield at the start of battle, and Tragedy! events pick another cat instead.
Why it fits: Answers the events that add curses (and several candidates do) at the cost of a pack slot forever.
Needs: new: loot that can't be removed

Name: Death's Scythe
Description: Stun 3 to every square around it. After you use it, lose 2 Health
Extra: Aim=any; Area=3x3; Type=Melee; Goal=Survive with exactly 1 Health; Charge=3
What it is there: A rare weapon won from Death: a spin attack for 13, after which the wielder is Doomed and goes down at the end of its turn.
Why it fits: A weapon with a price on every swing. Its goal is to cheat death, and the Death event candidate hands it out.

Name: Dead Cat
Description: You get 9 extra lives, but your Max Health becomes 1
What it is there: Sets Isaac's red heart containers to 1 and gives nine lives.
Why it fits: Isaac's most famous trade. The Felid candidate (nine lives) needs the same mechanic, so one build serves both.
Needs: new: extra lives

Name: Guppy's Collar
Description: Carry 3 pieces tagged guppy and become Guppy: every enemy you defeat leaves a fly that fights for you
What it is there: One of the Guppy items; picking up 3 of them transforms Isaac into his cat Guppy (flight, blue flies on every hit).
Why it fits: Transformations are Isaac's set bonuses; evolutions here need two pieces, and a three-piece set is the next step. Dead Cat carries the guppy tag too.
Needs: new: a set bonus for 3 pieces with a tag

Name: Mom's Purse
Description: A 1x1 bag. A trinket inside it counts as two pieces for its neighbours
What it is there: Lets Isaac carry two trinkets at once, and spawns a random trinket.
Why it fits: Trinkets are positional here; a purse that doubles one is the pack's version of an extra trinket slot.
Needs: new: a bag that changes what's inside it

Name: Glowing Hour Glass
Description: Use: undo your last report. The game you just played goes back to unplayed, and everything you gained or lost in it is restored
What it is there: Rewinds Isaac to the previous room and undoes everything that happened in the current one.
Why it fits: A real undo button for a bad evening, which only something with charges should give.
Needs: new: undoing a report

Name: Torch
Description: Use: for this game you are never in darkness. Used on a Shambler's Altar instead, it brings the Shambler
What it is there: A provision that raises the light meter, and the item curios want: on the Shambler's Altar it drops the light to 0 and summons the Shambler.
Why it fits: Light is a theme across several candidates (the Shambler, Darkness, the Miner Hat); the torch is the consumable version.

Name: Holy Water
Description: For your next game, you can't gain a Debuff
Extra: Preference=Positive
What it is there: A provision that raises the party's resistances to bleed, blight, disease and debuffs for 3 turns.
Why it fits: A cheap ward against the statuses here, the first thing that prevents rather than cures them.
Needs: new: blocking statuses

Name: Mountie Hockey Stick
Description: Stun 1 to the two squares in front; both are pushed back 1
Extra: Aim=front; Area=2x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Knock an enemy into another enemy; Charge=2
What it is there: The Mounties' special weapon: a hockey stick with much higher cleave and knockback than the ordinary one.
Why it fits: A wide knockback weapon; push already exists on the Hero Longsword, and the stick hits two at once.

Name: Adamantine
Description: Gain +2 Shields. Every Weapon in your pack Gains +1 Stun
What it is there: A rare, impossibly light and sharp metal found deep down; weapons and armour of it are the best in the game. Mining it is how forts dig too deep.
Why it fits: The best material in fantasy roguelikes, as a relic that helps armour and weapons at once.

Name: Golden Fleece
Description: Whenever you defeat an enemy, Gain +1 Strength. When you take damage, lose all of it, and take 1 more
What it is there: An unlockable fleece: +5% damage per kill, but hits deal double damage and reset the bonus.
Why it fits: A streak relic: the build grows until you're hit. Strength already exists as a status.

Name: Crush Curse
Description: When a game ends, destroy the piece this points at. Point it off the edge of the pack and it does nothing
What it is there: A negative bag curse found on items in low-rarity chests: it destroys the whole stack in the slot its arrow points at when you return to town.
Why it fits: The pack is already a position puzzle (Blueprint copies a neighbour); a piece that threatens one is the other side of that.
Needs: new: a piece that acts on its neighbour when a game ends

Name: Swap Curse
Description: When a game ends, the piece this points at becomes a copy of this one
What it is there: A positive bag curse: when you leave the dungeon, the stack it points at turns into copies of the cursed item.
Why it fits: A Blueprint that works once and permanently: pick what to sacrifice and what to duplicate.
Needs: new: turning one piece into another

Name: Unknown Curse
Description: This piece's name and effect are hidden until you finish a game while carrying it
What it is there: A negative bag curse: the item is hidden behind a question mark until you go home.
Why it fits: Identification already hides scrolls, potions, wands and pills; this would bring the gamble to any piece.
Needs: new: hiding an arbitrary piece

Name: Merchant Pendant
Description: Use: leave the game you're in without beating it. Pay 3 Gold; you keep everything you gained, and move on
What it is there: A one-way portal home from any dungeon floor, for a price that grows with the dungeon and the floor.
Why it fits: The rule is that you must beat a game to advance (spec §2); an expensive, one-use way out of a bad one is a real decision.
Needs: new: advancing without beating a game

Name: Merchant Mirror
Description: Use: sell a piece of loot for Gold: 1 for Common, 2 for Uncommon, 3 for Rare
What it is there: An unlockable mirror that turns items into gold for about a third of their base value.
Why it fits: Loot can be binned but never sold; a mirror turns the bin into income.
Needs: new: selling loot

Name: Polymorphine
Description: Drink: you are a Sheep until your next game (no verbs). Throw: the enemy on this tile becomes a Sheep: 1 Health, can't attack
Extra: Preference=Neutral; On Tile=the enemy here becomes a Sheep
What it is there: A pink, extremely dangerous liquid: a few pixels turn any creature into a helpless sheep.
Why it fits: Wand of Polymorph turns a body into another enemy; turning it into something harmless is a different, Noita-shaped joke with a dangerous drink side.
Needs: new: a Sheep body

Name: Doll
Description: Blocks the next 3 curses you would get, then breaks
What it is there: Blocks the next 2-4 curses the peasant receives; the Relic Altar resets its count.
Why it fits: Curses come from events here (add_curse); a piece that soaks a few is a different promise from Black Candle, which stops them for good.
Needs: new: blocking a curse

Name: Bounty Contract
Description: When a game starts, one enemy on the board is marked. Defeat it in that game: Gain +2 Gold
What it is there: Entering a room marks a random enemy with a spinning gold nugget; kill it before the timer and it drops gold (2% chance: a chest's worth).
Why it fits: The board already pays for kills; marking one body gives the player a target to plan around.
Needs: new: a marked body

Name: Tsar Bomba
Description: Whenever a Bomb defeats an enemy, Gain +2 Bombs. You deal 1 less damage for every 2 Bombs you hold
What it is there: Spawns two bombs whenever an enemy is killed with one, but takes 4 swing and throw damage off per bomb held.
Why it fits: A bomb snowball with a real cost: the more you hoard, the weaker you hit, so it wants spending.
Needs: new: a stat that scales with bombs held

Name: Bombushka
Description: When a Bomb explodes, it explodes again on 2 random tiles next to it
What it is there: A nesting-doll bomb: each bomb splits into three smaller bombs, which split again, all going off at once.
Why it fits: Brimstone Bombs spread the stun in lines; this one spreads the blast itself, at random.

Name: Pilfer Credit Card
Description: You can spend Gold you don't have, down to -5. While your Gold is below 0 you carry Debt: you can't buy anything until it's paid off
What it is there: Lets the peasant go into debt at the Pilfer Shop. A run ended in the red carries the Debt curse into the next one, and Debt blocks all buying until the balance is back to zero.
Why it fits: Shops sell for Gold and nothing lends it; a card that borrows from the future is a new shape of risk.
Needs: new: negative Gold, and the Debt curse

Name: Box of Holding
Description: Whenever you buy something in a shop, its slot restocks with the same kind of piece at double the price
What it is there: A gold sink: every item bought at the shop is restocked with one of the same type for 2^n times the price.
Why it fits: A shop that never runs dry, if you can afford it: turns spare Gold into more loot late in a run.
Needs: new: restocking a shelf

Name: Bottled Pilfer
Description: Drink: a Hoarding Pilfer stands up on the board; every hit on it pays 1 Gold, and it leaves after 2 turns. Throw: the same, on this tile
Extra: Preference=Positive; On Tile=a Hoarding Pilfer stands up here
What it is there: Spawns a rainbow Hoarding Pilfer, which drops Gold and Thorium when hit until it leaves. The wiki's advice: drink it somewhere safe and hit it until it goes.
Why it fits: A potion that puts a payout on the board instead of a buff, and it pairs with the Hoarding Pilfer goal row.
Needs: new: a body that pays per hit and leaves on a timer

Name: Canary
Description: When a game is beaten, Gain +1 Gold. After 3 games it grows: +2 instead
What it is there: The peasant's starting familiar, which collects gold. It levels up through a run; at level 3 it picks up gold quickly and even steals it back from Pilfers.
Why it fits: The Peasant's starting piece (candidate): a small, steady earner that gets better the longer it lives.
Needs: new: a piece that levels with games played

Name: Scroll of Enchanting
Description: Use: one piece in your pack gets +1 to its number: a trinket pays 1 more, a weapon stuns 1 more, a wand gains a charge
What it is there: The central item for character development, read like a skill point: almost every item benefits from enchanting, so you pour them into the few you mean to keep.
Why it fits: NetHack's Scroll of Enchant Weapon (candidate) only reaches weapons; Brogue's version reaches any piece, which is what makes it Brogue's.
Needs: new: a piece's number going up

Name: Potion of Detect Magic
Description: Drink: every unidentified piece you hold shows whether it is positive or negative. Throw: splashes harmlessly
Extra: Preference=Positive; On Tile=nothing (a good potion thrown just splashes)
What it is there: Marks every item in your pack (and on the level) blue for benevolent magic, red for malevolent, or a dash for none.
Why it fits: Unidentified potions, scrolls and wands already have a hidden Preference; this reads it without spending an identify.
Builds on: Preference, Scroll of Identify (live), NetHack Altar (candidate)

Name: Ring of Reaping
Description: Whenever you deal damage, Gain +1 Charge on a random chargeable piece
What it is there: Recharges your staves and charms by the physical damage you deal.
Why it fits: Charged Penny charges a piece when you gain Gold; this charges from fighting, so wands and weapons refill in the thick of it.

Name: Health Charm
Description: Use: Heal 2 Health. Then it needs 4 charges before it can be used again
What it is there: Heals a percentage of your maximum health, then must recharge; enchanting it heals more and recharges faster.
Why it fits: A healing item that comes back: charges already count defeated enemies (food), so it refills by fighting.

Name: Potion of Creeping Death
Description: Drink: Lichen grows on the tile in front of you. Throw: Lichen grows on this tile and the four around it
Extra: Preference=Negative; On Tile=Lichen on this tile and its 4 neighbours
What it is there: A malevolent potion that releases deadly lichen; thrown, it plants a lichen field that monsters refuse to cross.
Why it fits: The bad potion that's a weapon when thrown, as all Brogue's are; it brings the Lichen unit (candidate) with it.
Needs: new: the Lichen unit

Name: Wand of Beckoning
Description: Target Unit is pulled to the front column, and loses its next turn
What it is there: Yanks the target creature to the space next to you and delays its next move, so you can hit it as it lands.
Why it fits: The wands move bodies away (Teleportation); none brings one closer, which on this board means into reach.
Needs: new: pulling a body forward

Name: Staff of Discord
Description: Target Unit becomes Discorded for 2 turns: it attacks the enemies next to it instead of you
What it is there: Discords a monster: it attacks, and is attacked by, its allies. Funny against goblin conjurers and other summoners.
Why it fits: Nothing on the board turns enemies on each other; Discorded (status candidate) is that.
Needs: new: enemies attacking enemies

Name: Flawless
Description: Stun 3 to the front, until you take damage in a game; after that, Stun 1
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Clear a floor without taking damage; Charge=1
What it is there: A partisan that deals critical hits for as long as the player isn't hit, and becomes one of the weakest weapons once they are.
Why it fits: A weapon that rewards not getting touched, on a board where the bodies hit back.
Needs: new: a weapon whose Stun falls after damage

Name: Cursed Sword
Description: Stun 4 to the front. While it is in your pack you are Cursed
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Win a fight while one hit would kill you; Charge=1
What it is there: A sword with extremely high damage, constant critical hits and a fast swing, that keeps you Cursed (any hit kills) while it's equipped.
Why it fits: The strongest stun on the board, paid for by carrying a curse; it brings the Cursed curse (candidate) with it.
Needs: the Cursed curse (candidate)

Name: Dead Inside
Description: Double your Max Health. You can't heal
What it is there: A mutation that doubles maximum health but turns off every source of healing: the flask, food, Necromancy.
Why it fits: A trade the board doesn't offer yet: twice the health, none of it coming back.
Needs: new: blocking all healing

Name: Acceptance
Description: Curses lift twice as fast. Eating food gives you a random curse
What it is there: A mutation that halves the kills needed to lift a curse, but makes every food you eat curse you.
Why it fits: Ties the food family (9 pieces) to the curses: eat and get cursed, but shrug curses off quickly.
Needs: new: shortening a curse

Name: Get Rich Quick
Description: While you have Speed, every defeated enemy pays +1 Gold
What it is there: A mutation: enemies killed during a speed boost pay double gold, cashed in when the boost ends.
Why it fits: Speed is a live buff with nothing that pays for having it.

Name: Lich's Tome
Description: Your weapons Stun +1. Whenever you use one, a Bones stands up on the board
What it is there: A tier 3 item: +1 to every side of the hero's die, but every use of the die summons a Bones on the monsters' side.
Why it fits: Power with a body count: every swing feeds the board, and the Bones candidate is the body it feeds it.
Needs: new: a piece that spawns a body when a weapon is used

Name: Bond Certificate
Description: Does nothing until your 10th game ends. Then: Gain +10 Gold
What it is there: A tier 0 item: +15 to all the hero's sides, but only on turn 15.
Why it fits: A piece you carry for a long time for one big payday, which nothing in the pack does yet.
Needs: new: a piece that waits a set number of games

Name: Brittle Crown
Description: Whenever you defeat an enemy, Gain +1 Gold. Whenever you take damage, Lose 2 Gold
What it is there: A lunar item: hitting enemies sometimes pays gold, but taking damage surrenders a matching share of your gold to whatever hit you.
Why it fits: Piggy Bank pays you for getting hurt; this is the other way round, a crown that pays only while you don't get hit.

Name: Egocentrism
Description: At the start of each turn, Stun 1 a random enemy. When each game ends, a random piece in your pack becomes another Egocentrism
What it is there: A lunar item that keeps orbs circling you that home in on enemies, but every 60 seconds it eats one of your other items and becomes another stack of itself.
Why it fits: A piece that grows by eating the pack: strong, until it's all you have.
Needs: new: a piece that turns another into itself

Name: Gesture of the Drowned
Description: Your usable pieces recharge twice as fast, but each one uses itself as soon as it's ready
What it is there: A lunar item that halves equipment cooldown but fires the equipment the moment it's ready.
Why it fits: Charges are the pack's clock; this one halves it and takes away the choice of when.
Needs: new: pieces that use themselves

Name: Ceremonial Dagger
Description: Whenever an enemy is defeated, 1 damage to a random enemy
What it is there: When you kill an enemy, three spectral daggers appear where it died and home in on other enemies.
Why it fits: Kills that chain into kills: Gasoline leaves fire where a body dies, this sends the next blow on.

Name: The King's Gaze
Description: At the start of each game, only the pieces in the 3x3 around this one work, and they work twice
What it is there: The core mechanic: buildings only produce inside the area of the king's gaze, which you drag and rotate across the castle; the Monument to the King's Gaze keeps its neighbours running when the gaze is elsewhere.
Why it fits: Pack position already matters (Blueprint, bags). This makes it the whole point: you pick what the king is looking at.
Needs: new: pieces switched off by position

Name: Free Coupon
Description: The next piece you buy in a shop is free. Then this is used up
What it is there: An artifact: one item at the Trader at a 100% discount.
Why it fits: Shops are the place Gold goes; a one-time coupon is the simplest shop piece there is.
Needs: new: a discount on one purchase

Name: Blank
Description: Use: no enemy attacks this turn, and every enemy next to you is pushed back a tile
What it is there: A pickup: erases every enemy bullet in the room, stops enemies firing for a moment and pushes back everything near you. 'A last resort when dodge rolling has failed.'
Why it fits: The Gungeon's panic button: the board has stuns, but nothing that cancels a whole turn of attacks.
Needs: new: cancelling a turn of attacks

Name: Master Round
Description: When you defeat the board's boss without taking damage that game, Gain +1 Max Health
What it is there: Five variants, one per floor, each earned by beating that floor's boss without taking damage; each is a heart container.
Why it fits: A reward for a no-hit boss: it pairs with the Concierge's no-hit goal candidate (Dead Cells).
Needs: new: knowing whether you were hit this game

Name: Fusion Reactor
Description: Use, and choose: Fission — 1 to 3 random pieces get +1; or Fusion — two weapons in your pack become one piece, in one slot, that does both
What it is there: An item enemies sometimes drop. Fission grants random upgrade levels (or Gold if nothing can level); Fusion combines two maxed balls into one ball with both abilities, freeing a slot; Evolution turns set pairs into evolved balls.
Why it fits: Evolutions here need set ingredients; fusing any two weapons into one is the free-form version, and it frees pack space, which matters here.
Needs: new: fusing two pieces into one

Name: Cursed Second Wind
Description: When your Health would reach 0, you heal to 2 instead, and lose every other trinket in your pack
What it is there: A Cursed Blessing: on reaching 0 HP you are saved with 34% of your max HP, but lose all of your Blessings.
Why it fits: NetHack's Amulet of Life Saving (candidate) only costs itself; this one costs the whole build, which is a real decision.
Needs: new: surviving death

Name: Cursed Ammo
Description: Your weapons Stun +1, but each use costs 1 Gold
What it is there: A Cursed Blessing: each bullet fired also costs 200 Blood (the currency) but hits 50% harder.
Why it fits: Turns Gold into damage one swing at a time: the only piece that charges for each use.

Name: Mirror Match
Description: Bombs hit bosses after all: a boss takes double damage from a Bomb instead of ignoring it
What it is there: A charm from planting an Incubator pin: if a monster would be immune to your Attack Skill, it takes double damage instead.
Why it fits: Bosses here are bomb-immune; this turns the immunity inside out, which is exactly what the charm does.

Name: Wand of Skulltimate Greed
Description: Gold you gain is tripled. Everything in shops costs double
What it is there: A boss relic that triples the gold found in battles and doubles the cost of every purchase: slightly more spending power, and a lot more for anything that counts your gold.
Why it fits: Gold pieces here count how much Gold you hold (To the Moon pays per 3 held); this swells the number without swelling what it buys.
Needs: new: a price multiplier

Name: Bee Hive
Description: Stun 1 to a random enemy, three times a swing
Extra: Aim=random; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Set a swarm of insects on an enemy; Charge=3
What it is there: A gun that fires bees that home in on enemies, sting on impact and leave a lingering swarm that keeps hurting.
Why it fits: Three random strikes a swing is a weapon the board doesn't have: Lightning Ring earns its extra strikes, this starts with them.

Name: Casey
Description: Stun 2 to the front, then push right 2. While it is in your pack you carry a random curse
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Hit an enemy with a bat or a club; Charge=3
What it is there: A baseball bat: a charged swing hits everything nearby and reflects bullets, and enemies it kills are launched into the others. It adds 2 Curse.
Why it fits: The big push is the home run; the curse is the price the Gungeon charges for it.

Name: Snowballer
Description: Stun 1, and +1 for every 2 columns between you and where it lands
Extra: Aim=any; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Hit an enemy with a snowball; Charge=3
What it is there: Fires snowballs that slowly freeze what they hit.
Why it fits: A weapon that is better at range: the board's back columns are usually the hardest to reach.
Needs: new: Stun that grows with distance

Name: Camera
Description: Stun 1 to every enemy on the board
Extra: Aim=none; Area=board; Type=Ranged; Goal=Take a photo of an enemy; Charge=3
What it is there: Fires a charged flash that deals 10 damage to every enemy in the room.
Why it fits: The only weapon that touches the whole board: weak, but nothing hides from it.

Name: Blasphemy
Description: Stun 1 to the front. At full Health it also fires a sword beam: Stun 1 to the whole row
Extra: Aim=front; Area=2x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Fire a sword beam while at full health; Charge=3
What it is there: The Bullet's starting sword: a wide swing that destroys bullets, and a piercing rainbow sword projectile, but only at full health.
Why it fits: The Zelda sword beam, kept exactly: it rewards staying unhurt.
Needs: new: a weapon that reads your Health

Name: Mailbox
Description: Stun 1 to one enemy. Every third swing is a package: Stun 2 in a 3x3
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Deliver a letter or a package; Charge=3
What it is there: Fires mail; the last shot in each magazine is a package that explodes, scatters glitter, burns or poisons. (Killing a boss covered in glitter is the 'Day Ruiner' achievement.)
Why it fits: A weapon with a rhythm: two small swings, then a big one.
Needs: new: a weapon that counts its swings

Name: Honeycomb
Description: Whenever you take damage, Stun 1 three random enemies
What it is there: A passive item: taking damage releases 10-20 bees that seek out enemies.
Why it fits: A trinket that answers getting hurt, and Bee Hive's evolution partner.

Name: Bomberpal
Description: Stun 1 in a plus, twice a swing
Extra: Requirement 1=Lil' Bomber; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "bomb"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: A synergy: with a Bomb, Lil' Bomber fires two bombs instead of one, charges twice as fast and reloads 40% faster.
Why it fits: Lil' Bomber already evolves into King Bomber with a crown; this is its other branch, through the bomb family (5 live pieces). Same weapon, two futures, which is what the Gungeon's synergies feel like.
Builds on: Lil' Bomber (live), the bomb tag, King Bomber's evolution

Name: BEES
Description: Stun 2 to a random enemy, three times a swing
Extra: Requirement 1=Bee Hive; Requirement 2=Honeycomb; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: A synergy: with Honeycomb or Bumbullets, Bee Hive's bees are twice the size and deal 25% more damage, at a slower rate of fire.
Why it fits: Both halves are candidates here (Bee Hive, Honeycomb), so it comes as a set.

Name: Frosty the Bullet Tyrant
Description: Stun 1, and +1 for every column between you and where it lands; it hits a plus
Extra: Requirement 1=Snowballer; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "snow"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: A synergy: with Frost Bullets, Snowballer's shots grow in size and damage the further they travel.
Why it fits: Snowballs that roll and grow, unlocked by the snow family (1 live piece, so it also gives that family a reason).

Name: Earthquake
Description: Stun 1 to everything in a 3x3
Extra: Aim=any; Area=3x3; Type=Ranged; Goal=Cause an earthquake; Charge=3
What it is there: A base ball, the Makeshift Sisyphus's and the Tunneller's starter: each hit deals damage to every unit in a 3x3 square around it.
Why it fits: The board has 3x3 potions but no 3x3 weapon; it is also the Makeshift Sisyphus candidate's starting piece.

Name: Egg Sac
Description: Stun 1 to one enemy, then it bursts: Stun 1 to 2 random enemies
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Hit an enemy with a shot that bounced off a wall first; Charge=3
What it is there: A base ball, the Flagellant's starter: it explodes into 2-4 baby balls on hitting an enemy, then needs 3 seconds before it can be shot again.
Why it fits: One aimed strike that becomes random ones: the brick-breaker's bounce, in this board's words.
Needs: new: a weapon that adds random strikes after an aimed one

Name: Fireworks
Description: Stun 1 to 3-6 random enemies, and each gets 1 Burn
Extra: Requirement 1=Egg Sac; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "fire"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: An evolved ball (Burn + Egg Sac): explodes into 3-6 fireworks that seek random enemies and set them alight.
Why it fits: Ball x Pit evolves by fusing two balls; here the second ball is the fire family (4 live pieces), which says the same thing.
Builds on: Egg Sac (candidate), the fire tag, Burn

Name: Drill
Description: Stun 1 to every enemy in the row, front to back, and +1 to the last
Extra: Requirement 1=Earthquake; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "stone"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: An evolved ball (Earthquake + Iron): pierces enemies and deals bonus damage until it reaches the back of the field.
Why it fits: The original's second ball is Iron; the nearest live family is stone (3 pieces). A drill through the whole row is a shape no weapon has.

Name: Ratau's Staff
Description: Stun 1 to the front. Every enemy it hits gives a random chargeable piece +1 Charge
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with nothing better than a stick; Charge=3
What it is there: 'Barely more than a stick': the weakest weapon in the game, whose hits make enemies drop Fervour, the power Curses spend. Ratau, the Lamb's mentor, carried it.
Why it fits: A poor weapon that feeds the others: its stun is the least, but each hit charges something else.

Name: Godly Sword
Description: Stun 3 to the front
Extra: Requirement 1=Wooden Sword; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "holy"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: A Godly Weapon (unlocked as a doctrine): 'Deal significantly more damage than mortal weapons.' Every weapon kind has a Godly version.
Why it fits: A mortal sword made divine by something holy. This crosses games (Backpack Battles' Wooden Sword becoming Cult of the Lamb's Godly Sword), so it's the owner's call; the holy family has 1 live piece.

Name: Broom Spear
Description: Stun 1 to the two squares in front of you
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x2; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with a broom, a mop or a frying pan; Charge=3
What it is there: Will's starting weapon: 'A tool with one, simple purpose. To clean. At least, that is if held in untrained hands.'
Why it fits: A starter weapon with a joke in it and a long reach; it is what the Golem Drill Spear is forged from.

Name: Golem Drill Spear
Description: Stun 2 to the three squares in a line in front of you
Extra: Requirement 1=Broom Spear; Requirement 2=Any 2 Items or Trinkets with "whetstone"; Outcome=Consume All
What it is there: Forged at Vulcan's Forge from a Training Spear, 10 Whetstones and 4 Golem Chisels: a drill-headed spear 'made incredibly hard to pierce through rock'. It's the spear from Gurren Lagann.
Why it fits: Moonlighter's forge upgrades a weapon with materials, which is what an evolution is here, and its recipe names whetstones, already a live family (the Hero swords evolve through them).
Builds on: Broom Spear (candidate), the whetstone tag, Hero Longsword's recipe

Name: Vorpal Blade
Description: Stun 1 to the front. 1 swing in 20 beheads: the enemy it hits is defeated outright (not a boss)
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Behead an enemy; Charge=3
What it is there: A neutral artifact long sword, the default crowning gift for most neutral heroes: it can behead what it hits.
Why it fits: Its goal is the live Jabberwock's on purpose: 'One, two! One, two! And through and through / The vorpal blade went snicker-snack!' A weapon and the monster it was made for, sharing one goal.
Needs: new: a chance to defeat outright

Name: Mjollnir
Description: Stun 1 to one enemy, and lightning arcs to Stun 1 another at random. It comes back
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Defeat an enemy with a lightning bolt; Charge=3
What it is there: A neutral artifact war hammer, the Valkyrie's first sacrifice gift: it strikes with lightning and, thrown by a strong enough Valkyrie, returns to her hand.
Why it fits: A thrown weapon that returns, with a lightning arc. Its goal is the lightning family's (Lightning Ring and Thunder Loop share it), so the hammer joins that family; the catch went to Don't Starve's Boomerang, the purer example.

Name: Singing Sword
Description: Stun 1 to the front. 1 swing in 4 it sings: Stun 1 to every enemy on the board
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Make so much noise that every enemy comes for you; Charge=3
What it is there: An unrandart double sword that talks: each hit may cast Sonic Wave on everything in sight, louder and stronger the tenser the fight. At its loudest it is the Screaming Sword; silenced, the Sulking Sword.
Why it fits: A sword that occasionally hits the whole board, and a goal about the noise it makes.
Needs: new: a chance for a weapon to hit the board

Name: Plutonium Sword
Description: Stun 2 to the front. 1 swing in 5 the enemy it hits mutates: it becomes a random enemy of the same difficulty
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Get mutated; Charge=3
What it is there: An unrandart triple sword: 20% of strikes malmutate, deal extra damage or polymorph the target, and putting it away leaves you magically contaminated.
Why it fits: Wand of Polymorph (live) on the end of a sword, with the risk that the new body is worse.

Name: Rapier
Description: Stun 3, but only to an enemy in column 2: a lunge across the empty square in front of you
Extra: Aim=column 2; Area=cell; Type=Melee; Goal=Lunge at an enemy from two steps away; Charge=3
What it is there: A light sword whose lunge, made by stepping toward an enemy across one empty square, always hits and deals triple damage; good against ogres, who are off balance after they swing.
Why it fits: A weapon that wants a gap: strong, but only at one distance.

Name: War Axe
Description: Stun 1 to every enemy in the front column
Extra: Aim=front; Area=col; Type=Melee; Goal=Hit every enemy around you with one swing; Charge=3
What it is there: A heavy axe (19 strength) that attacks every adjacent enemy at once, which makes being surrounded much less dangerous.
Why it fits: The front column is where the board's bodies crowd you; this clears it in one swing.

Name: The Butcher's Cleaver
Description: Stun 2 to the front. Every enemy it defeats leaves meat: Gain a random food
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Defeat an enemy with a cleaver or an axe; Charge=3
What it is there: The Butcher's unique axe in Diablo I: 'a nightmarish amalgam of blood, bone and steel', still smelling of fresh meat decades later.
Why it fits: The Butcher's goal candidate greets you with 'Ah, fresh meat!'; his cleaver turns kills into food for the food family (9 live pieces).
Builds on: enemy_killed, food tag, The Butcher (goal candidate)

Name: Boomerang
Description: Stun 1 to one enemy, and it comes back. 1 swing in 4 you fumble the catch: take 1 damage
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Throw a weapon and catch it again; Charge=3
What it is there: A craftable ranged weapon that returns after it's thrown; you have to catch it, or it hits you, loses twice the durability and lands on the ground.
Why it fits: A ranged weapon with a cost you can mess up: the catch is the whole idea.

Name: Dark Sword
Description: Stun 3 to the front. While it is in your pack, you start every game with 1 less Health
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Lose your mind; Charge=3
What it is there: A magical sword made from Nightmare Fuel and a Living Log, one of Maxwell's starting items: 68 damage a hit, among the strongest in the game, and it drains Sanity the whole time it's held.
Why it fits: Strength paid for every game it's carried, the way Don't Starve charges sanity for it.
Needs: new: a weapon with a carrying cost

Name: Chainsaw
Description: Stun 1 to the whole front column, three times a swing. Thirsty: it needs 4 charges, not 3
Extra: Aim=front; Area=col; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with a power tool; Charge=4
What it is there: A motorized weapon: hold the button and it attacks continuously, and it can be swung around, but it burns through its fuel fast, so it's for emergencies.
Why it fits: The zombie-film weapon: the most damage in the front column, paid for with an extra charge (its fuel).

Name: Balanced Blade
Description: Stun 1 to the front, and +1 for every swing in a row this run (up to +3). Taking damage resets it
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Land ten hits in a row without being hit; Charge=3
What it is there: A fast sword whose damage climbs with each consecutive hit, and which crits after ten.
Why it fits: A weapon that grows while you stay clean: Flawless (candidate) is all-or-nothing, this one builds up.
Needs: new: a weapon that remembers its streak

Name: Spite Sword
Description: Stun 1 to the front, or Stun 3 if you took damage this game or carry a curse
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Strike back at the enemy that just hit you; Charge=3
What it is there: A sword that crits for a while after you take damage, or while you're cursed.
Why it fits: Flawless's opposite, from the same game: it wants you hurt. With the curses here, it's a reason to keep one.
Needs: new: a weapon that reads this game's damage

Name: Vampire Killer
Description: Stun 1 in a 3x1 that ignores shields, and every enemy it defeats leaves the Fire tile
Extra: Requirement 1=Whip; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "fire"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: Return to Castlevania DLC: the Belmonts' whip, with far-reaching attacks that bypass shields, crit burning enemies and start fires on a kill.
Why it fits: The live Whip (Vampire Survivors, itself a Castlevania homage) already becomes Bloody Tear through a heart; this is its other branch, through fire, into the whip it was always imitating.
Builds on: Whip (live), Bloody Tear's evolution, the fire tag, the Fire tile, pierce_shields

Name: Bouldorb
Description: Stun 1 to every enemy in a row, front to back, except flying ones (bat and fly tags)
Extra: Aim=front; Area=row; Type=Ranged; Goal=Roll a boulder into an enemy; Charge=3
What it is there: The biggest orb in the game: it hits more pegs at once and its attack pierces every enemy, but it can only hit enemies on the ground. A boulder + orb portmanteau, like every orb name.
Why it fits: A piercing row attack with a gap in it: the board's flying bodies (Bullat, King Bullat, flies) go free.
Needs: new: a weapon that skips a tag

Name: Bear Traps
Description: Lay a Bear Trap on an empty tile: the first enemy to step on it is Stunned 2
Extra: Aim=any; Area=cell; Type=Ranged; Goal=Trap an enemy in place; Charge=3
What it is there: An uncommon weapon with 6 uses: each places a Bear Trap on an open tile 1 to 5 squares away. Placed in water, every connected water tile fills with traps.
Why it fits: A weapon that sets the board instead of hitting it. Its goal is the live Spider Kitten's, from the same game: trapping something in place.
Builds on: Spider Kitten (live) and its goal, Landmine and Cage Trap units
Needs: new: a Bear Trap unit

Name: Bloody Bear Traps
Description: Lay a Bear Trap on an empty tile (Stun 2), and it needs only 2 charges
Extra: Requirement 1=Bear Traps; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "blood"; Outcome=Consume None
What it is there: A very rare weapon from the corpse of the Throbbing King: the same trap with infinite uses, one of Mewgenics' 'Bloody' upgrades (Bloody Knife, Bloody Stick, Bloody Spikes...).
Why it fits: Mewgenics' Bloody versions are its own evolutions, and the blood family is already live (6 pieces).

Name: Vibro blade
Description: Stun 2 to the front, ignoring shields. It needs an energy cell: 4 charges, not 3
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with a weapon that runs on batteries; Charge=4
What it is there: A vibro long sword: powered by an energy cell, its strikes match the target's armour value, so they almost always penetrate; each strike spends 100 charge.
Why it fits: The only weapon here that ignores shields, at the cost of a fourth charge for its battery.

Name: Royal Capacitor
Description: Stun 2 to one enemy, and Stun 1 to the squares around it: a lightning strike
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=plus; Type=Ranged; Goal=Defeat an enemy with a lightning bolt; Charge=3
What it is there: An equipment: a reticle locks onto the monster nearest your cursor, and activating it calls a lightning strike down on it half a second later, dealing 3000% damage and stunning everything nearby.
Why it fits: RoR2 has no weapons, but its equipment is aimed and recharges, which is what a weapon is here. It joins the lightning family's shared goal (Lightning Ring, Thunder Loop).

Name: Brimstone
Description: Stun 2 to every enemy in a row: a blood laser through everything
Extra: Aim=front; Area=row; Type=Ranged; Goal=Fire a laser that goes through everything; Charge=3
What it is there: A passive item that triples damage and turns tears into a charged laser that pierces everything in its path, enemies, hazards and walls, hitting twice.
Why it fits: The most famous of Isaac's tear-replacers. The live Brimstone Bombs already borrows its name; this is the laser itself.

Name: Mom's Knife
Description: Stun 2 to the whole row, then it comes back: Stun 1 to the front
Extra: Aim=front; Area=row; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with a kitchen knife; Charge=3
What it is there: Tears are replaced by a single penetrating knife that can be held as a melee blade (often killing non-boss enemies outright) or thrown, dealing triple damage on the way out and returning.
Why it fits: The mom family is already live (3 pieces) and has no weapon; her knife is the obvious one.

Name: Kapala
Description: Every 8 enemies defeated: Gain +1 Health
What it is there: A chalice made from a human skull, Kali's gift at 16 favour: it fills with blood, yours or anyone's, and every eight drops it gives a heart.
Why it fits: Healing that comes from the fighting; Infusion (live) adds empty Max Health per kill, this fills it.

Name: Web Gun
Description: Apply the Web tile to the target and the squares around it. No Stun of its own
Extra: Aim=any; Area=plus; Type=Ranged; Goal=Shoot a web or a net at an enemy; Charge=3
What it is there: A ranged weapon that launches blobs of goo that become webs; it does no damage but holds enemies, and is the second cheapest item in the shops.
Why it fits: The Web tile is live and only Sticky Bombs lay it; this lays a plus of it and hurts nothing.

Name: Mattock
Description: Stun 1 to the front, and destroy a unit or object on that square
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Dig through a wall; Charge=3
What it is there: A digging tool that makes a decent weapon: one of the few things that can destroy blocks, for treasure and shortcuts. Always buried under the left ruby in a snake pit.
Why it fits: A weapon that clears the board's placed things (traps, turrets, rocks) as well as hitting.
Needs: new: a weapon that destroys units

Name: Stygian Blade
Description: Stun 1 to the front. Every third swing also bursts: Stun 1 to every square around it
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Attack straight out of a dash; Charge=3
What it is there: Stygius, Blade of the Underworld: Zagreus's starting weapon, a longsword with wide and directional swings and an area special that roots you briefly.
Why it fits: The starter blade of the best-known action roguelike; its Hidden Aspect makes it Excalibur (evolution candidate).
Needs: new: a weapon that counts its swings (as Mailbox)

Name: Heart-Seeking Bow
Description: Stun 1 to one enemy anywhere, and the one behind it
Extra: Aim=enemy; Area=1x2; Type=Ranged; Goal=Release a shot at exactly the right moment; Charge=3
What it is there: Coronacht: a charged shot that pierces, worth 10 extra damage if released at the perfect moment; the special sprays arrows in a cone.
Why it fits: A long-range, piercing weapon; its goal is the bow's perfect release.

Name: Shield of Chaos
Description: Stun 1 to three random enemies, then it comes back. Passive: the first hit you'd take each game is blocked
Extra: Aim=random; Area=cell; Type=Melee; Goal=Throw a shield; Charge=3
What it is there: Aegis: swing in an arc, hold to block anything from the front, release to bash; the special throws it to bounce between enemies and return.
Why it fits: A shield that's also a thrown weapon: the only weapon here with a defensive passive.
Needs: new: a weapon passive that blocks

Name: Excalibur
Description: Stun 2 to the front and the squares around it: Arthur's hallowed ground
Extra: Requirement 1=Stygian Blade; Requirement 2=Any Item or Trinket with "blood"; Outcome=Consume All
What it is there: Titan Blood reveals the Stygian Blade's Hidden Aspect of Arthur, which turns it into Excalibur, raising hallowed ground around Zagreus.
Why it fits: Hades' aspects are its evolutions, paid in Titan Blood; the blood family (6 live pieces) is the nearest thing. NetHack's Excalibur is already a weapon candidate, so this could land on it.
Builds on: Stygian Blade (candidate), the blood tag, NetHack's Excalibur (weapon candidate)

Name: Frying Pan
Description: Stun 1 to the front, and 1 Burn
Extra: Aim=front; Area=1x1; Type=Melee; Goal=Fight with a broom, a mop or a frying pan; Charge=3
What it is there: The Chef's weapon: every hit applies Burn (the Artisan passive), and the pan can bat fireballs back. The Chef's Stew heals and recharges by collecting health drops.
Why it fits: Shares Moonlighter's Broom Spear goal on purpose: a household weapon. Burn on hit gives the board a second Burn source beside Fire.

Name: Bone Saw

Description: At the start of each game, Gain +1 Temporary Shield for every 5 empty cells in your pack
What it is there: A relic that gives extra Block each turn for every 5 empty spaces in your backpack.
Why it fits: The first piece that rewards leaving room in the pack, from the game the pack was built on. It joins the wood family (5 live).
Builds on: the pack's empty cells, Temporary Shield, wood tag
Needs: new: counting empty cells

Name: Beast's Ring
Description: Melee weapons next to it Gain +1 Stun. At the start of each game, take 1 Damage
What it is there: A cursed ring: adjacent Melee Weapons get +1 damage, and each turn it hurts you for 1. 'He who haunts the dungeon.'
Why it fits: The Whetstone's neighbour bonus with a price on it, and a ring (3 live).

Name: Evil Hand
Description: After each game, it pulls each piece next to it one cell closer. A piece that can't move is destroyed, and you Gain +1 Strength
What it is there: A cursed item: each turn it pulls items closer; an item that can't move closer is destroyed, and the Hand grows stronger for it. 'Here's your new home.'
Why it fits: A piece that moves the others around the pack and eats what it can't move, which is the whole point of where a piece sits.
Needs: new: a piece that moves other pieces

Name: Ring of Peace
Description: Gain +1 Empty Max Health. Every board starts with one fewer enemy, and bosses come as their weakest kind
What it is there: A ring: an extra empty heart container while worn, 1 enemy removed per room on every new level, and minibosses spawn as their weakest variant.
Why it fits: A ring that makes every fight a little smaller, which nothing in the pack does yet. It joins the ring family (3 live).
Needs: new: removing a body from the starting board

Name: Crown of Greed
Description: All Gold you gain is doubled, but you lose 1 Gold after every game
What it is there: Headwear that doubles all gold pickups and drains 1 gold per beat; it only drops from killing the Shopkeeper, and it instantly kills the Monk.
Why it fits: More money, always leaking. As a crown it also turns Lil' Bomber into King Bomber (crown has 1 live piece).
Builds on: gold_gained, lose_gold, crown tag (King Bomber's evolution)

Name: Monkey's Paw
Description: Every enemy with the monkey tag is Stunned for as long as it stands on the board
What it is there: An item worn without a slot: all monkeys, water balls and gorgons become permanently frozen. The game's monkeys grab you and stop you moving.
Why it fits: The answer to the live Monkey enemy, which came from this game. A tag-specific piece is a new kind of counter.
